newsitem.title: CANADA: Toronto stocks hit new high on post-holiday gains.
newsitem.headline: Toronto stocks hit new high on post-holiday gains.

text.p: Toronto's key 300 index finished at record highs on Tuesday as Canadian stocks caught up to Monday's strong rally in New York.
Trading was heavy as investors returned from the Thanksgiving holiday which left Canadian financial markets closed on Monday.
The TSE 300 Composite Index rose 19.40 points to a record close of 5480.60 on volume of 82.2 million shares worth C$1.2 billion ($886 million).
The TSE also set an intra-day peak of 5495.91.
But the overall market was mixed. Declines outnumbered advances 479 to 461 with 308 issues unchanged.
"We're seeing a carry over from yesterday and Toronto is trying to catch up," said Ira Katzin, an investment adviser with Richardson Greenshields of Canada Ltd.
The Dow Jones Industrial Average broke through the 6000-point barrier on Monday and stayed above 6000 on Tuesday despite afternoon profit-taking.
On the TSE, conglomerates led 11 of 14 sub-groups higher. Other strong sectors included communications, oil and gas, utilities and merchandising.
But these gains were partly offset by losses in consumer products and precious metals.
* Stampeder Exploration Ltd. jumped 0.55 to 6.35 on 4.9 million shares as energy stocks surged on higher oil prices.
Stampeder's activity was also due to arbitragers settling accounts after the company's C$512 million ($378 million) takeover of Morgan Hydrocarbons Inc.
Among other energy issues, Talisman Energy Inc. climbed 0.65 to 39.40, while Renaissance Energy Ltd. improved 0.95 to 42.45.
* Gold miner Bre-X Minerals Ltd. fell 0.55 to 22.95 on 1.9 million shares. Bre-X earlier rejected an Australian company's claim to a piece of Bre-X's huge Indonesian gold property.
* Canadian banks were active as well. Bank of Montreal added 0.15 to 39.90 on 1.3 million shares. Canada's third-largest bank said it will announce a major banking initiative on Wednesday.
Among other banks, Royal Bank of Canada added 0.40 to 42.05 on 1.3 million shares.

Toronto-Dominion Bank bucked the trend, falling 0.25 to 30 on 1.2 million shares. T-D bank earlier today closed its C$715 million ($528 million) takeover of U.S. discount broker Waterhouse Investor Services Inc.
